title: Vendor Emergency Sequestration & Legal Hold Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is a vendor-facing contractual exhibit and internal operational runbook describing steps Redwood and a contracted vendor will take to immediately sequester and preserve data, perform a chain-of-custody for evidence, and implement a legal hold in response to suspected exfiltration, regulatory request, or legal process. It is intended to be included as an annex to vendor agreements (SaaS, hosting, managed services) and to align technical, legal, and SRE teams on responsibilities and timelines.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all vendors that process customer-identifiable inputs or inference outputs on behalf of Redwood or Redwood customers, including hosted, dedicated, and private deployment vendors.
- Not intended to replace broader DPA obligations; it supplements the DPA with emergency evidence and sequestration mechanics.
- Activates on notice from Redwood legal, security, or compliance teams or as required by court order/regulatory notice.

Activation criteria (examples):
- Confirmed data exfiltration or unauthorized access affecting Redwood customer data.
- Preservation request from Redwood Legal due to subpoena, litigation hold, or regulatory audit.
- Sudden vendor compromise where forensics cannot be performed without immediate snapshotting/sequestration.

High-level vendor obligations (contract annex language suggested):
1) Immediate preservation and isolation: Upon written notice or lawful process, the Vendor shall:
   a) Immediately preserve all logs, configuration, backups, snapshots, KMS key metadata, and object storage objects relevant to the impacted tenants for a minimum of 180 days or per Redwood instruction.
   b) Isolate impacted compute instances/storage volumes to prevent further writes while maintaining read-only access for forensic analysis.
   c) Take an immutable snapshot of object stores, block volumes, and container images relevant to the event and provide an unaltered cryptographic hash (SHA-256) for each artifact to Redwood within 4 hours of activation.

2) Chain-of-custody and evidence handling:
   a) Vendor must maintain a chain-of-custody log for each preserved artifact including timestamp, personnel, operation performed, and cryptographic hash.
   b) Any transfer of preserved artifacts to third parties (including Redwood or law enforcement) must be logged and accompanied by signed acknowledgment.

3) Key material and encryption:
   a) If vendor manages encryption keys, vendor shall immediately (on request) produce a key escrow snapshot or provide a sealed key-wrapping artifact to enable decryption for forensic review under Redwood supervision.
   b) Vendor must not rotate or destroy any keys related to the preserved artifacts without express written agreement from Redwood.

4) Access and temporary privileged accounts:
   a) Vendor will create a time-limited, auditable read-only account scoped to the preserved artifacts for Redwood SRE or a mutually agreed third-party forensic vendor.
   b) Vendor agrees to provide secure remote session logs, recorded session artifacts, and all elevated access tokens used during the investigation.

5) Logs and telemetry retention:
   a) Vendor must preserve full application, network, audit, and orchestration logs (minimum retention 90 days) spanning 30 days prior and 30 days after the incident start time unless Redwood specifies otherwise.
   b) If log sampling or retention policies would cause loss of critical telemetry, vendor must disable sampling for impacted tenants and preserve complete streams immediately.

6) Communication and coordination:
   a) Vendor shall designate a single technical liaison and one legal point-of-contact reachable 24/7 via phone/SMS and email for the duration of the preservation period.
   b) Initial acknowledgement: Vendor must acknowledge receipt of preservation notice within 1 hour and confirm initial preservation actions within 4 hours.
   c) Status cadence: vendor will provide written status updates at 4-hour intervals for the first 48 hours, then daily unless escalated.

7) Evidence access, export, and return:
   a) Redwood may request secure export of preserved artifacts. Vendor shall provide a tamper-evident export package (e.g., signed tarball with accompanying manifest and SHA-256 hashes) and transfer logs within 48 hours of request.
   b) After Redwood confirms receipt and forensics are complete, vendor shall retain originals for 180 days or per Redwood instruction, unless a court order dictates different handling.

8) Cost and third-party labs:
   a) Vendor shall bear reasonable costs of immediate preservation actions for incidents resulting from vendor negligence or security failures.
   b) For incidents where vendor is not at fault, cost-sharing terms will be negotiated in good faith; the contract should define a default cost-recovery mechanism.

9) Non-disclosure and confidentiality:
   a) All artifacts and communications under this playbook are Confidential. Vendor must limit access on a least-privilege basis and prohibit disclosure except as required by law.

10) Audit and verification rights:
   a) Redwood reserves the right to obtain third-party forensic verification of preserved artifacts. Vendor must cooperate and provide access to verify hashes, timestamps, and preservation procedures.

Operational runbook (internal step-by-step checklist for activation):
- T0 (trigger): Legal/Security issues preservation notice to vendor via registered notice channel and posts JIRA-INC ticket.
- T0+1h: Vendor acknowledges receipt (SC contact). Document time and contact in ticket.
- T0+4h: Vendor provides artifact manifest with hashes and initial isolation confirmation. If not provided, escalate to Vendor SOC lead and Redwood Legal.
- T0+6h: Redwood SRE and vendor coordinate secure session access; create read-only forensic account.
- T0+12h: Verify snapshot integrity (hashes) and begin prioritized forensic imaging (customer-impacting tenants first).
- T0+24-72h: Provide interim forensic notes and evidence packages for legal review; discuss cost responsibilities and next steps.
- T0+72h+: Transition to standard investigation cadence and legal preservation as directed.

Minimum technical artifacts to preserve (non-exhaustive):
- Full object storage snapshots for affected buckets (with version history).
- Block device snapshots (immutable) for affected instances.
- Database logical dumps and binary logs (wal/redo segments) covering 7 days around incident.
- Orchestration metadata (pod manifests, container images, deployment history).
- KMS metadata, key IDs, rotation logs, and any HSM attestations.
- System and application logs, auditd outputs, process lists, and kernel ring buffers as available.

Forensics and redaction rules:
- Redwood will identify data subject identifiers (DSI) and provide redaction scope to vendor if required by privacy obligations.
- Vendor should provide a copy of raw artifacts to Redwood; redaction should only be performed under explicit written direction from Redwood Legal.

Cross-border and data sovereignty considerations:
- If preserved artifacts contain cross-border data, vendor must notify Redwood within the initial 4-hour window and provide proposed storage location and transfer protections.
- Vendor must not transfer artifacts to a jurisdiction that would impede Redwood’s access or conflict with contractual data residency commitments without prior Redwood approval or lawful compulsion.

Dispute resolution & escalation:
- If vendor fails to comply with preservation requests, Redwood may seek injunctive relief and audit access per contract.
- Escalation path: Vendor SOC → Vendor CISO → Redwood Security Director → Redwood General Counsel.

Template invocation clause (contract text to include in agreements):
"Upon written notice from Redwood, Vendor shall comply with Redwood’s Vendor Emergency Sequestration & Legal Hold Playbook (Exhibit X), which is incorporated by reference and shall supersede any conflicting vendor retention or deletion policy for preserved artifacts. Failure to comply constitutes a material breach enabling Redwood to obtain immediate equitable relief and recover documented preservation costs where vendor negligence is demonstrated."

Practical negotiation points to watch for in vendor review:
- Time-to-hash and snapshot SLAs (target: 4 hours but vendors may request 24–48 hours for large scale).
- Costs for snapshot storage and forensic exports — negotiate cap or default Redwood payment with reconciliation.
- KMS access: vendors often resist key escrow; consider HSM-assisted key shares or escrow under strict access controls.
- Jurisdictional restrictions: require pre-approved cross-border handling plans in SOWs for private deployments.

Appendix A: Example preservation notice template (to vendor)
To: [Vendor SOC contact]
Subject: Preservation Notice — [Redwood Customer/Project] — Activation of Vendor Emergency Sequestration & Legal Hold Playbook
Body: Redwood Legal and Security request immediate preservation and isolation of all artifacts related to [brief summary]. Please acknowledge within 1 hour and provide initial preservation manifest (hashes + timestamp) within 4 hours. Point-of-contact: [Redwood Legal contact + phone]. This notice activates Exhibit X per contract.

Appendix B: Chain-of-custody form (fields)
- Artifact ID
- Artifact type
- Hash (SHA-256)
- Timestamp taken (UTC)
- Operator name and role
- Operation performed (snapshot, export, transfer)
- Transfer recipient and signature
- Comments/flags

Review notes and next steps:
- Draft annex for legal review and pilot with two vendors (one hosted SaaS, one Dedicated hosting partner) to validate timings and export packaging.
- Align SRE runbooks with vendor technical contacts and add playbook to incident tabletop exercises.
- Confirm cost recovery defaults with Finance for recurring preservation events.

Owner and maintenance:
- Document owner: Maya Patel, Security & Compliance.
- Review cadence: annually and after any major incident.

Document history:
- 2024-11-07: Initial draft (Maya Patel).
- 2024-12-12: Added KMS key-handling options (Luis Ortega).
- 2025-02-12: Incorporated feedback from Legal; changed acknowledgement SLA to 1 hour (Priya Ramanathan).

End of document.
